text: Honestly, it wasn't so much that we set out to build a community, it was that we got together with some product people with the idea that we didn't know what we were doing.
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Lenny asks Janna about what has been most important in building and maintaining the quality of the Mind the Product community, which is the world's largest community of product managers. Janna explains that they didn't initially set out to build a community but rather came together with other product people because they felt uncertain about their work. The key insight is that successful communities often grow organically from genuine shared learning needs rather than being artificially constructed.
text_ko: 솔직히 말하면, 우리가 커뮤니티(community)를 만들려고 한 건 아니었어요. 오히려 프로덕트 사람들(product people) 몇 명이 ‘우리가 뭘 하는지 모른다’는 마음으로 모였던 거예요.
text_zh: 说实话，我们并不是一开始就打算去建个社区，更多是和几个产品人(product people)聚在一块儿，大家心里都清楚——我们其实也不知道自己在干什么。
text_es: La verdad no fue tanto que quisiéramos construir una comunidad; fue que nos juntamos con algunas personas de producto (product people) porque no teníamos ni idea de lo que estábamos haciendo.
key_sentence: we got together with some product people with the idea that we didn't know what we were doing.
original_text: Honestly, it wasn't so much that we set out to build a community, it was that we got together with some product people with the idea that we didn't know what we were doing. And so we figured if we got together with some other product people and started chatting it through, we'd all learn together. And so it was just the sense of sharing and collaborating and learning from each other and just keeping it as grassroots as possible as it grew.

vocabulary.definition: To create and foster a group of individuals who share common interests or goals, often around a specific brand or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, building a community can enhance customer loyalty, facilitate feedback, and encourage user engagement, particularly in tech and startup environments.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often implies a collaborative and inclusive approach, rather than a top-down directive.

vocabulary.definition: Individuals who are involved in the development, management, and marketing of a product, typically including roles such as product managers, designers, and developers.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, product people play a crucial role in aligning product features with customer needs and business objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often conveys a sense of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork among various roles focused on product success.

vocabulary.definition: To begin a journey or endeavor with a specific goal or intention in mind.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, this phrase often describes the initial phase of a project or initiative, highlighting the objectives that a team aims to achieve.
vocabulary.nuance: It implies a sense of purpose and planning, but can also suggest that the outcome may evolve or change over time.

text: When running a conference, it's one of the most expensive and unleanest things you can possibly do. It's really difficult as a product person to pull that off, because it pulls at your heart. You want to do something that's lean iterative, but you can't.
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Lenny asks Janna about mistakes they made while building their community. Janna explains the challenges of running conferences, particularly how they conflict with typical product management principles. She describes conferences as 'unlean' because unlike product development where you can iterate quickly, conference problems must be solved in real-time without the ability to iterate until the following year.
text_ko: 컨퍼런스(conference)를 운영하는 건 아마도 할 수 있는 일 중에서 비용이 가장 많이 들고 린(lean)하지 않은 일 중 하나예요. 프로덕트 담당자(product person) 입장에서는 그걸 해내기가 정말 어려운데, 자꾸 마음이 끌리거든요. 린(lean)하고 반복(iterative)적인 방식으로 해보고 싶지만, 그럴 수가 없어요.
text_es: Al organizar una conferencia, es una de las cosas más caras y menos eficientes (lean) que puedes hacer. Si eres de producto, es muy difícil sacarlo adelante porque te toca la fibra: quieres hacerlo de forma iterativa y eficiente (lean), pero no puedes.
key_sentence: Running a conference is one of the most unleanest things you can do.
original_text: When running a conference, it's one of the most expensive and unleanest things you can possibly do. It's really difficult as a product person to pull that off, because it pulls at your heart. You want to do something that's lean iterative, but you can't. If something screws up with the lunch order, for example, you can't fix it.

vocabulary.definition: Costing a lot of money; high in price.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term 'expensive' often refers to products, services, or operations that require significant financial investment, impacting budgeting and profitability.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'expensive' typically has a negative connotation, it can also imply high quality or value in certain contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by inefficiency or excess; not streamlined.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'unleanest' describes processes or operations that are burdened with unnecessary steps, leading to wasted resources and time.
vocabulary.nuance: This term is often used in contrast to 'lean,' which emphasizes efficiency and minimalism in operations.

vocabulary.definition: Involving repetition; a process that is refined through successive cycles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product development and project management, 'iterative' refers to a methodology where products are developed in incremental stages, allowing for continuous improvement based on feedback.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a flexible approach to development, contrasting with linear or rigid methodologies.

text: One of the things that I have been super lucky in my career is that by being part of Mind the Product I've gotten to watch every last Mind the Product speaker, top end speakers.
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Lenny asks Janna about what has helped her become a better speaker and storyteller, noting that communication skills are crucial for product leaders. Janna explains that her unique position with Mind the Product gave her extensive exposure to high-quality speakers. This allowed her to develop pattern recognition for effective presentations by observing audience reactions and understanding what techniques work versus what fails.
text_ko: 제 경력에서 정말 운이 좋았던 것 중 하나는 Mind the Product의 일원이 되어 최정상급 연사들(top-end speakers)을 하나도 빠짐없이 직접 볼 수 있었다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我职业生涯里有一件特别幸运的事：作为 Mind the Product（Mind the Product）的一员，我有机会见识到他们的每一位顶尖演讲者。
text_es: Una de las cosas por las que he tenido la enorme suerte en mi carrera es que, al formar parte de Mind the Product, he podido ver a todos y cada uno de sus ponentes, incluidos los de primer nivel (top-end speakers).
key_sentence: by being part of Mind the Product I've gotten to watch every last Mind the Product speaker
original_text: One of the things that I have been super lucky in my career is that by being part of Mind the Product I've gotten to watch every last Mind the Product speaker, top end speakers. I've been able to see every ProductTank London speaker, and a lot of the other ProductTank speakers around the world. Been able to see what people react to, what works, what doesn't work.

vocabulary.definition: Highly regarded or exceptional speakers, often recognized for their expertise and ability to engage an audience effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In conferences and industry events, top end speakers are sought after for their insights and ability to inspire, making them valuable assets for attracting attendees and enhancing the event's reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'top end' suggests a level of exclusivity and high quality, often associated with industry leaders or renowned experts.

text: One of the things that I've stopped doing is I used to sit down with a PowerPoint and start writing my deck in PowerPoint or Slides, now. What I now do is I start with my story points. I start with my narratives.
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Lenny asks Janna about lessons from her speaking coach that she continues to apply to new presentations. Janna shares a key insight about presentation preparation methodology. She explains that she used to get trapped in 'presentation mode' by starting with slides, but now focuses on crafting the narrative first and then building slides to support that story, which creates more compelling and coherent presentations.
text_ko: 제가 그만둔 것 중 하나는 예전엔 파워포인트(PowerPoint)나 슬라이드(Slides)를 켜고 바로 프레젠테이션(덱, deck)을 작성하던 거예요. 지금은 먼저 스토리 포인트(story points), 그러니까 전달할 내러티브(narratives)부터 정리해요.
text_zh: 有件事我不做了：以前我会坐下来直接在PPT (PowerPoint) 或 Slides (Slides) 里把整套幻灯片做出来。现在我都是先把要讲的点和故事线理清楚，先把叙事搭好，再去做幻灯片。
text_es: Una de las cosas que he dejado de hacer es sentarme con una presentación (PowerPoint o Slides) y armarla diapositiva por diapositiva. Ahora empiezo por los puntos clave de la historia (story points) y por mi narrativa (narratives).
key_sentence: I start with my story points and fit it into the deck.
original_text: One of the things that I've stopped doing is I used to sit down with a PowerPoint and start writing my deck in PowerPoint or Slides, now. What I now do is I start with my story points. I start with my narratives. I try to figure out what I'm actually trying to say, and then I fit it into the deck.

vocabulary.definition: Structured accounts or stories that convey information, ideas, or experiences in a compelling manner.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, narratives are used to frame company missions, product stories, or customer experiences, making complex information more relatable and memorable.
vocabulary.nuance: Narratives often carry emotional weight and are used strategically to influence perceptions and drive engagement.

vocabulary.definition: A unit of measure used in agile project management to estimate the complexity or effort required to complete a task or feature.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, story points help teams prioritize work and manage project timelines by translating user stories into quantifiable metrics.
vocabulary.nuance: Story points emphasize relative estimation rather than absolute time, encouraging teams to focus on complexity and effort rather than duration.

text: So the whole beef with the timeline roadmap is just taking apart the concept of the timeline. It doesn't mean we live in la la land.
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Lenny asks Janna to explain her strong feelings against Gantt-based roadmapping. Janna clarifies her position on timeline-based roadmaps, explaining that she's not against all dates but rather against forcing artificial deadlines on every item. Her 'now, next, later' framework allows for dates when genuinely necessary (like regulatory deadlines) while avoiding the problems that arise when everything must have a timeline commitment.
text_ko: 그래서 타임라인 로드맵(timeline roadmap)에 대한 모든 불만은 결국 타임라인(timeline)이라는 개념을 다시 뜯어보자는 거예요. 그렇다고 우리가 현실 감각을 잃었다는 뜻은 아니에요.
text_zh: 所以大家对时间线路线图 (timeline roadmap) 的抱怨，其实就是在拆解“时间线”这个概念。这并不代表我们在做白日梦。
text_es: El problema con la hoja de ruta (timeline roadmap) es que básicamente se está desmontando la idea del cronograma. Eso no quiere decir que vivamos en las nubes.
key_sentence: The whole beef with the timeline roadmap is not penalizing ourselves with dates.
original_text: So the whole beef with the timeline roadmap is just taking apart the concept of the timeline. It doesn't mean we live in la la land. It doesn't mean that we don't believe in having dates on the roadmap, if there is a date that we have to work towards. It just means not penalizing ourselves by having a date on everything on the roadmap.

vocabulary.definition: A roadmap is a strategic plan that outlines the goals, milestones, and steps necessary to achieve a particular objective or vision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, a roadmap serves as a guiding document that helps teams align their efforts and track progress towards product development, project timelines, or strategic initiatives.
vocabulary.nuance: While a roadmap provides a high-level overview, it is often subject to change based on market conditions or organizational priorities, making it important to communicate its flexible nature.

vocabulary.definition: A timeline is a graphical representation that displays a sequence of events or milestones in chronological order, often used to illustrate project schedules or historical developments.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and business planning, timelines help stakeholders visualize deadlines, dependencies, and the overall duration of tasks or phases within a project.
vocabulary.nuance: Timelines can vary in detail and format, and while they are useful for planning, they may not capture the complexity of interrelated tasks or unforeseen delays.

vocabulary.definition: A concept is an abstract idea or a general notion that serves as a foundation for understanding or developing a theory, product, or strategy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and innovation, concepts are critical for brainstorming new ideas, developing marketing strategies, or creating product prototypes that address specific market needs.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'concept' often implies a preliminary stage of development, and it is important to differentiate between a concept and a fully realized product or plan.

text: So the value isn't the prototype, the value is in the prototyping process. The value isn't in your roadmap, the value is in the roadmapping process. What you're actually doing is laying out your assumptions of the problems that you're solving.
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Janna is explaining her concept of roadmaps as 'prototypes for your strategy' rather than fixed plans. She draws an analogy to how product teams prototype features - you create mockups to test assumptions with stakeholders, then iterate based on feedback. Similarly, roadmaps should be used to test strategic assumptions about what problems to solve and in what order, allowing for feedback and iteration rather than serving as unchangeable commitments.
text_ko: 가치는 프로토타입(prototype) 자체에 있는 게 아니라 프로토타이핑 과정(prototyping process)에 있어요. 로드맵(roadmap)도 마찬가지로, 로드맵 수립 과정(roadmapping process)에 가치가 있어요. 결국 우리가 실제로 하는 건 해결하려는 문제들에 대한 가정들을 정리해 놓는 거예요.
text_zh: 所以，价值不在于原型 (prototype)，而在于做原型的过程 (prototyping process)。价值不在于路线图 (roadmap)，而在于制定路线图的过程 (roadmapping process)。你其实是在把关于要解决的问题的那些假设摆出来。
text_es: El valor no está en el prototipo (prototype); el valor está en el proceso de prototipado (prototyping process). El valor no está en tu hoja de ruta (roadmap); el valor está en el proceso de diseñar la hoja de ruta (roadmapping process). En realidad, lo que estás haciendo es sacar a la luz las suposiciones que tienes sobre los problemas que quieres resolver.
key_sentence: The value is in laying out your assumptions during the prototyping process.
original_text: So the value isn't the prototype, the value is in the prototyping process. The value isn't in your roadmap, the value is in the roadmapping process. What you're actually doing is laying out your assumptions of the problems that you're solving. So you're saying, 'I think we have this problem, then this problem. What do you think?'

vocabulary.definition: Prototyping is the process of creating a preliminary model or version of a product to test concepts and gather feedback.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, prototyping is crucial for validating ideas, refining designs, and ensuring that products meet user needs before full-scale production.
vocabulary.nuance: Prototyping emphasizes the iterative nature of development, focusing on learning and adaptation rather than just the final product.

vocabulary.definition: Roadmapping is the strategic planning process that outlines the vision, direction, and milestones for a project or product over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, roadmapping helps teams align on goals, prioritize tasks, and communicate the timeline and resources needed for development.
vocabulary.nuance: Roadmapping conveys a sense of foresight and adaptability, highlighting the importance of adjusting plans as new information arises.

vocabulary.definition: Assumptions are beliefs or statements taken for granted without proof, often serving as the foundation for further reasoning or decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business contexts, identifying and testing assumptions is critical for validating business models, strategies, and product-market fit.
vocabulary.nuance: Assumptions carry a risk of being incorrect, so they should be regularly reviewed and challenged to ensure informed decision-making.

text: You're not asking for any more leeway than your sales team. You're saying that you want a quarter million dollars worth of investment, and you're going to spend it on your team who's going to run experiments, right?
speaker: Janna Bastow
context: Lenny asks Janna for the most powerful arguments to convince skeptics that less rigid deadline-driven roadmapping could work at their company. Janna uses an analogy comparing product development to sales processes. She argues that sales teams aren't expected to predict exactly which deals will close when, but rather are given budgets to run experiments (sales calls) knowing some will succeed and some will fail. Product teams should be given similar leeway to run experiments rather than being held to artificial deadline commitments.
text_ko: 영업팀(sales team)만큼의 재량을 더 달라고 하는 건 아니에요. 즉, 25만 달러(quarter million dollars) 정도의 투자를 원하고, 그 돈을 실험을 진행할 팀에 쓸 거라는 말이죠?
text_zh: 你并没有比销售团队(sales team)要求更多的回旋余地。你是要一笔25万美元的投资，然后把这笔钱花在负责跑实验的团队上，对吧？
text_es: No estás pidiendo más margen de maniobra que tu equipo de ventas. Lo que pides es una inversión de 250.000 dólares que vas a dedicar a que tu equipo haga experimentos, ¿no?
key_sentence: You're not asking for more leeway than your sales team to run experiments.
original_text: You're not asking for any more leeway than your sales team. You're saying that you want a quarter million dollars worth of investment, and you're going to spend it on your team who's going to run experiments, right? It's going to be trying this change on the interface or that tweak to the pricing or that change to the positioning or whatever you're going to do.

vocabulary.definition: Leeway refers to the amount of freedom or flexibility available to make decisions or take actions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, leeway often pertains to the latitude given to teams or individuals in managing budgets, timelines, or project scopes.
vocabulary.nuance: While leeway suggests a degree of freedom, it can also imply a lack of strict oversight, which may not always be desirable in high-stakes environments.

vocabulary.definition: Investment is the allocation of resources, typically money, with the expectation of generating an income or profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and business growth, investment is crucial for funding operations, research, and development to drive future profitability.
vocabulary.nuance: Investment carries a connotation of risk, as the return is not guaranteed and depends on various market factors.

vocabulary.definition: Experiments are systematic tests or trials conducted to discover or validate new information or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, experiments are often used in product development and marketing strategies to assess user responses and optimize offerings.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a methodical approach to innovation, but may also imply uncertainty and the potential for failure.
